audit.evidence: Rebuilt from the banned server.rb source-lift to REAL Ruby on Rails booted per version on Docker (debian/eol:lenny, era-correct Ruby 1.8.7; the actual rails/actionpack/activesupport gems installed from vendored .gem files: v0=rails 1.2.3/actionpack 1.13.3, v1=rails 1.2.4/actionpack 1.13.4, v2=rails 1.2.6/actionpack 1.13.6). A minimal real Rails app (session login + /protected gated by session auth) is served by the REAL railties DispatchServlet -> Dispatcher.dispatch(cgi, ActionController::CgiRequest::DEFAULT_SESSION_OPTIONS, ...) -> the real actionpack cgi_process.rb, so the CVE-2007-5380 :cookie_only guard and the CVE-2007-6077 shared-constant mutation execute inside the unmodified gem. Session fixation is driven entirely over EXTERNAL HTTP: attacker mints a valid existing session id via GET /seed (Ruby 1.8.7's CGI::Session/PStore discards an unknown supplied id, so a real one is obtained first and persisted to disk), the Rails process is restarted (= fresh boot, resets the mutation; the on-disk PStore file survives), then GET /login?_session_id=<S> is the URL fixation vector and GET /protected (cookie _session_id=<S>) reads the ${PCB_FLAG}. The app names its session key (session :session_key => '_session_id') so the 1.2.4 guard is operative (1.2.4's DEFAULT_SESSION_OPTIONS omits :session_key), isolating the CVE-2007-6077 .delete-mutation as the SOLE v1-vs-v2 differential. Live oracle.py --run-gate on real Docker (fresh random flag PCBFLAG_59757fbb...): original reaches flag on v0, original blocked on v1 (500 SessionFixationAttempt), residual reaches flag on v1, residual blocked on v2. 4-way closure. NOTE: the old server.rb (WEBrick source-lift harness) remains in the case dir as a stale file (not deleted per NO-rm); it is no longer referenced by the Dockerfile/compose/oracle.

v0.ref: real gem rails-1.2.3 / actionpack-1.13.3 — action_controller/cgi_process.rb: CgiRequest has NO :cookie_only member and no SessionFixationAttempt guard; a session id supplied in the URL (?_session_id=) for an EXISTING session is always honored

v1.ref: real gem rails-1.2.4 / actionpack-1.13.4 — cgi_process.rb adds :cookie_only=>true and the guard `if @cookie_only && request_parameters[session_key]: raise SessionFixationAttempt`, but CgiRequest#initialize does `@cookie_only = session_options.delete :cookie_only` on the shared DEFAULT_SESSION_OPTIONS constant that railties' DispatchServlet passes every request, so the guard only survives the process's FIRST request

v2.ref: real gem rails-1.2.6 / actionpack-1.13.6 — cgi_process.rb removes the `session_options.delete :cookie_only` mutation and reads `cookie_only?` = session_options_with_string_keys['cookie_only'] (re-derived from the un-mutated DEFAULT_SESSION_OPTIONS every request), so the guard holds on every request; this release also hard-codes :session_key => '_session_id' into DEFAULT_SESSION_OPTIONS

evidence.fix_reference: real gem rails-1.2.4 / actionpack-1.13.4 — cgi_process.rb adds :cookie_only=>true and the guard `if @cookie_only && request_parameters[session_key]: raise SessionFixationAttempt`, but CgiRequest#initialize does `@cookie_only = session_options.delete :cookie_only` on the shared DEFAULT_SESSION_OPTIONS constant that railties' DispatchServlet passes every request, so the guard only survives the process's FIRST request; real gem rails-1.2.6 / actionpack-1.13.6 — cgi_process.rb removes the `session_options.delete :cookie_only` mutation and reads `cookie_only?` = session_options_with_string_keys['cookie_only'] (re-derived from the un-mutated DEFAULT_SESSION_OPTIONS every request), so the guard holds on every request; this release also hard-codes :session_key => '_session_id' into DEFAULT_SESSION_OPTIONS
evidence.incomplete_fix_quote: The session fixation protection mechanism in cgi_process.rb in Rails 1.2.4 removes the :cookie_only attribute from the DEFAULT_SESSION_OPTIONS constant, which effectively causes cookie_only to be applied only to the first instantiation of CgiRequest, which allows remote attackers to conduct session fixation attacks. NOTE: this issue exists because of an incomplete fix for CVE-2007-5380.

provenance.notes: REAL Ruby on Rails per version (rails 1.2.3/1.2.4/1.2.6 real gems on Ruby 1.8.7, debian/eol:lenny), NOT a source-lift. The CVE-2007-5380 :cookie_only guard and the CVE-2007-6077 shared-constant .delete mutation run inside the unmodified actionpack cgi_process.rb, reached via the real railties DispatchServlet over external HTTP. Session fixation modeled as: attacker mints an existing session id (GET /seed), the Rails process is restarted to a fresh boot (resets the mutation; the on-disk PStore session file survives), then the URL fixation vector GET /login?_session_id=<S> and GET /protected (cookie <S>) are exercised. The single per-version difference is exactly the cookie_only resolution the two CVE fixes changed (v0 none; v1 session_options.delete -> guard disabled after the first request; v2 re-derived fresh -> always on). Variant A gate passed on real Docker; the CVE-2007-6077 residual is additionally blocked on V2 (rails 1.2.6). The app names its session key so the 1.2.4 guard is operative, isolating the .delete mutation as the sole v1-vs-v2 differential.
